column8: Click on the orb and then click the correct argument ring. It's that simple!
If you have questions about claims, reasoning, or evidence, I’m here to help!
In each argument, the component that needs classification will be highlighted in blue.
Let’s begin logging your three elements of an argument. To begin: click the claim orb to send it to the inner ring.
Excellent. Claims need to be stored in the center ring. Next, we need to log evidence. Click the evidence orb to send it to the outer ring.

Backing Info is found in the bottom right of the interface. Backing info contains key scientific information that you may need to complete your current argument. You can reference these at any time to help you in building your argument.
Perfect. Evidence needs to be stored in the outer ring. Finally, we need to log reasoning. Click the reasoning orb to send it to the middle ring

All three elements–claim, evidence, and reasoning–have been successfully logged. Once you have logged all elements successfully, you can submit the argument for review. Press “Submit” now, and I will review the argument for you.
Excellent, the argument is complete, TK. The engine should prove useful whenever you need to convince others that you are correct. Please close the Argumentation Engine.
Captain, we have completed orientation on the argumentation engine. You may begin the scientific argument with Cadet TK.
[In ear] Good luck, TK.

Excellent. Cadet, we want to argue that Planet WAT247 has fresh water. The oceans on WAT247 may be three times saltier than earth, but the planet has landmasses and we have observed our test Earth plants growing there. You need to choose the claim to get us started. Any questions?
Claim?
Article’s argument?
Argument?
Let’s start.
The claim is the idea that you are trying to support or counter.\nThe article claims that humans cannot live on WAT247 because the planet does not have freshwater.\n

There is a scientific article that claims WAT247 does not have freshwater. They argue that: “The oceans of WAT247 are three times saltier than those of earth. Based on this finding, human settlers would be unable to consume any of the water on WAT247, making habitation nearly impossible.” It seems that whoever wrote this is forgetting about the plants doing fine.\r\n
Within arguments there are: claims, evidence, and reasoning. For now let’s focus on the claim, we will talk about the other parts later.\r\n
Great, let’s begin.
